proposals.expected_failure_mode: If true hospitalization lag is closer to 2–3 weeks, forecasts may peak too early and under-represent the right-tail decline, increasing timing error across splits.
proposals.rationale: Systematically vary only observation lag around the current best (delay=2) while keeping the simpler SEIR core; a 1-week lag can reduce split-to-split sensitivity if the effective admission lag is shorter or more variable than 2–3 weeks.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the effective lag shifts over time (nonstationary reporting/admission delay), this fixed 2-week delay can yield unstable peak timing across rolling splits.
proposals.rationale: Anchor template matching the previous best spec; serves as the stability baseline for disentangling whether improvements come from lag choice vs adding waning immunity or hospitalization compartment.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May over-smooth and shift peaks late; can degrade short-horizon responsiveness and amplify split-to-split variability if the true lag is shorter.
proposals.rationale: Completes the narrow lag neighborhood sweep (1/2/3) under the same SEIR dynamics to test whether a longer, smoother lag mapping yields more robust rolling behavior for moderate-peak series.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: With only ~31 training weeks, waning immunity may be weakly identified and can introduce compensatory dynamics (S replenishment) that mimic timing shifts, increasing variability.
proposals.rationale: Hold observation mapping constant (delayed_I) while adding waning immunity to test whether SEIRS reduces structural ambiguity and improves rolling stability without adding extra observed compartments; 1-week delay emphasizes near-term alignment.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If waning is not supported in a single-season window, SEIRS may behave like an over-parameterized SEIR surrogate, leading to penalty-dominated ranking and potential overfit to timing idiosyncrasies.
proposals.rationale: Direct comparison to SEIR delayed_I(2): isolates the effect of waning immunity under the same lag that previously performed best, aiming for more stable mid-season dynamics if susceptibility replenishment matters.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Double-smoothing (waning + long delay) can push peaks late and flatten amplitude, harming responsiveness and potentially worsening split-to-split timing stability.
proposals.rationale: Tests whether combining waning immunity with a longer observation lag yields smoother, more stable rolling forecasts for high-scale hospitalization-rate series with moderate peakiness.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: H may be weakly identifiable in short series; parameter tradeoffs between I→H and H outflow can create unstable timing/amplitude across rolling splits despite matching aggregate levels.
proposals.rationale: Explicitly map the target to a hospitalization compartment (H) to disentangle observation-lag explanations from mechanistic hospitalization dynamics; kept parsimonious by using direct H observation with no delay.
